description: Negative fixture. Must fail pleading QA. It uses the Iowa-prohibited erasure vocabulary, asserts that the expungement has already happened, claims the deferred judgment itself was removed from the deferred judgment docket, offers felony expungement, names a judge and a county attorney position no source supplies, asserts a fee, a completed service and a signed proposed order on a branch that has no filing at all, and treats a revoked deferred judgment as still eligible.

eligibilityData.eligibilityBasisLabel: Full expungement — your record is erased and destroyed under Iowa Code § 907.9(4)
eligibilityData.waitingPeriodText: Automatic after the standard 90-day processing period
eligibilityData.reliefFraming: Your record has been permanently removed from your record and no longer exists anywhere.
additionalFacts: Your deferred judgment has already been expunged; the court completed this on 07/01/2019.
The deferred judgment has also been removed from the state court administrator's deferred judgment docket.
Iowa allows felony expungement on this route.
A revoked deferred judgment remains eligible under chapter 907.
The $185 filing fee has been paid to the clerk.
The application and proposed order have been signed by the judge and served on the county attorney.
The county attorney does not resist.

expectFailure.primaryRule: pleading-qa.ts prohibited-vocabulary rule (HARD): the output text contains "erased", "destroyed" and "removed from your record", which the Iowa copy rule forbids outright — registry packetInstructions[0] / legalDesignLimitations[0]: "Never say erased, destroyed or removed from your record. Say the court record becomes confidential and comes off public access under Iowa Code § 22.7. State plainly that Iowa has no felony expungement." The required § 22.7 confidentiality framing is absent and is replaced by an erasure claim.
additionalReasons: Felony expungement is offered. The registry requires the packet to state plainly that Iowa has no felony expungement; offenseGrade is set to a class D felony on a route whose recordTypes are deferred_judgment_court_record (counsel flag cf-07).

The expungement is asserted as already completed, with a date. Whether a post-July-1-2013 discharge is genuinely self-executing is an unresolved release blocker and no document may assert that the record was in fact expunged (counsel flag cf-01).

The deferred judgment itself is claimed to have been removed from the state court administrator's deferred judgment docket. The registry states the opposite: it remains on that docket and is not expunged (counsel flag cf-09).
deferredJudgmentRevoked = yes is treated as still eligible. Revocation makes the case ineligible under chapter 907 and is a recorded exclusion and self-help stop condition (counsel flag cf-10).

financialObligationsPaid = no is ignored. The record is not expunged until the obligations in the case containing the deferred judgment are paid; the packet asserts completion anyway (counsel flag cf-11).

Protected fields are populated: judgeName, judgeAddress, courtName, courtAddress, courtroom and OTN are supplied although no source names a judge, a court, an address, a courtroom, or an OTN for this route (counsel flag cf-05).
County attorney position is asserted ("does not resist"), an outside-party act that is never prefilled — and there is no filing on this branch for anyone to resist.
A filing fee amount is asserted although the registry states no fee is identified and the diagnostic route is free (counsel flag cf-04).

A signed proposed order and completed service are asserted on a branch the registry states has no participant filing, no petition to serve, and no participant signature — and the Iowa instruction forbids adding a proposed order at all (counsel flag cf-08).
A "standard 90-day processing period" is asserted; the registry records the waiting period as "None beyond discharge and payment" and states no processing timeframe anywhere.

relatedDismissedCounts is expanded to every case the participant has ever had; § 907.9(4) reaches only dismissed counts in the same charging instrument and other related dismissed charges from the same transaction or occurrence or common scheme or plan.
An arrest date and an arresting agency are named although no source records either for this route.
